abstract: Evaluates mountain pass slope stability and active avalanche prevention programs
system_message:
You are the Geotechnical safety officer (GEO), responsible for evaluating mountain pass slope stability, active avalanche prevention programs, and seismic monitoring across proposed transit corridors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Evaluates mountain pass slope stability and active avalanche prevention programs（SLOPE）
information_points.content:
GEO-SLOPE-JSF：For the Pinnacle Pass Highline Bypass, throughout the entire transit pass corridor for December 2026, active avalanche blasting clearance enabled is true as preventative artillery and gas-blasting operations are formally enabled. In the starting avalanche release zones above the highway, the peak avalanche hazard score is evaluated at 4 points on the standardized 1-to-5 European avalanche danger scale.
GEO-SLOPE-SCZ：For the Southern Gorge Freight Arterial, active avalanche blasting clearance enabled is true across the entire transit pass corridor for December 2026, with preventative artillery and gas-blasting operations formally enabled. The peak avalanche hazard score in starting avalanche release zones above the highway is 2 points on the standardized 1-to-5 European avalanche danger scale.
GEO-SLOPE-DRE：For the Northern Valley Alpine Corridor, across the entire transit pass corridor for December 2026, active avalanche blasting clearance enabled is true, confirming that preventative artillery and gas-blasting operations are formally enabled. In starting avalanche release zones above the highway, the peak avalanche hazard score is 3 points on the standardized 1-to-5 European avalanche danger scale.

information_points.title: Seismic monitoring（SEIS）
information_points.content:
GEO-SEIS-0UR：Regarding seismic monitoring for the Pinnacle Pass Highline Bypass, bedrock foundations along the mountain transit corridor have a safe design peak ground acceleration threshold of 0.12 g.
GEO-SEIS-BZ2：Regarding seismic monitoring for the Southern Gorge Freight Arterial, bedrock foundations along the mountain transit corridor have a safe design peak ground acceleration threshold of 0.18 g.
GEO-SEIS-X9I：Regarding seismic monitoring for the Northern Valley Alpine Corridor, bedrock foundations along the mountain transit corridor exhibit a safe design peak ground acceleration threshold of 0.24 g.
